final.answer: The transmitter feeding FIC-10-1 is FT-10-1 (a Rosemount 3051, HART 4-20 mA version). It has no fixed failure direction: on a detected sensor or microprocessor failure the 4-20 mA signal is driven either high or low, and which of the two applies is user-selectable via a jumper/switch on the transmitter [p. 88]. The alarm levels depend on the configuration: standard default is high ≥ 21.75 mA and low ≤ 3.75 mA, NAMUR-compliant (option codes C4/CN) is high ≥ 22.5 mA and low ≤ 3.6 mA, and custom levels (option codes CR/CS, or CT for standard low) can be set at ordering time within 20.2–23.0 mA high and 3.6–3.8 mA low. To change the alarm direction you use that jumper/switch on the transmitter, but the available facts do not describe the step-by-step procedure for doing so.

final.answer: The valve operated by control loop FIC-11-1 is FV-11-1, a Fisher ET/EAT globe valve. Seal and ring materials available for it include: PTFE seal rings (PTFE V-ring packing and PTFE/composition plug seals, rated about -73 to 232 °C / -100 to 450 °F; some PTFE V-ring constructions span -101 to 316 °C / -150 to 600 °F with appropriate construction); PTFE/graphite (or PTFE/carbon) seal rings, which may be used with PEEK anti-extrusion rings up to 316 °C / 600 °F in non-oxidizing service or 260 °C / 500 °F in oxidizing service (standard limit 232 °C / 450 °F, extendable above 232 °C / 450 °F only with PEEK rings and spring-loaded seal rings); spring-loaded valve plug seals in PTFE with N10276 spring (approx. -73 to 232 °C / -100 to 450 °F), S30200, S31600 or S41600 stainless steel, or PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring (up to 316 °C / 600 °F for oxidizing service per its note); UHMWPE (R30003) seal rings on ET trim (trim temperature limit -198 to 66 °C / -325 to 150 °F with the 316 SST/ENC cage); and Ethylene-propylene (-40 to 232 °C / -40 to 450 °F), Fluorocarbon (-18 to 204 °C / 0 to 400 °F, not for steam or ammonia), Nitrile (max 71-82 °C / 160-180 °F, for air and hydrocarbons or compatible fluids), and Carbon-filled PTFE (-73 to 232 °C / -100 to 450 °F) for the 2-piece valve plug seal. Supporting rings are made of N05500 (load ring), N07750 (retaining ring for spring-loaded seal ring construction), and PEEK (anti-extrusion rings). Packing options are ENVIRO-SEAL PTFE (standard, max 232 °C / 450 °F), ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF (up to 316 °C / 600 °F, 104 bar / 1500 psig) and ENVIRO-SEAL duplex; graphite ribbon/filament packing is rated -18 to 316 °C / 0 to 600 °F.

final.answer: The transmitter measuring E-16-1 is FT-16-2, a Rosemount 3051-series transmitter. The data does not pin down a single process connection for it; the entries show several possibilities depending on the exact model/option: 1/2-14 NPT female (Rosemount 3051T), 1/4-18 NPT or 1/2-14 NPT on 2-, 2 1/8- or 2 1/4-inch centers (Rosemount 3051C coplanar), and for the 3051L a flanged high-pressure side with a low-pressure side of 1/4-18 NPT on the flange or 1/2-14 NPT on the adapter. So a 1/4 NPT connection is among the documented options but is not confirmed as the fitted one. Integral manifolds are available with this transmitter family: assemble-to options include the Rosemount 305 Integral Manifold (option S5), the Rosemount 304 Manifold (S6), the Rosemount 306 Integral Manifold, plus direct-mount 3-valve and 5-valve manifold configurations (integral or remote-mount, in SST or alloy C-276), so yes, it can be obtained with a manifold already fitted.

final.answer: FT-11-1 (a Rosemount 3051 flow transmitter) is tested per IEC 60770-1:1999 for the 'field or pipeline with high vibration level' condition: 0.21 mm peak displacement from 10-60 Hz and 3 g acceleration from 60-2000 Hz. Under that test, the effect on the reading is less than ±0.1 percent of URL (the top of the calibrated span). Note these are test levels and their effect on measurement error; no separate general vibration endurance or shipping vibration rating is given.

final.answer: GV-12-3 is described as a Type 165 2/2-way solenoid valve, so yes, it needs electrical power. The documentation lists available supply voltages of 24V DC, 230V AC 50/60Hz, and 115V AC 50/60Hz, with a voltage tolerance of ±10%. So 24 V DC will work — you do not need 230 V AC; either is acceptable depending on which coil variant is fitted. Note power consumption is 5 W (DC) or about 20 VA inrush / 11 VA (5 W) holding for AC, connection is via a cable plug (IP65), and you should match the voltage/current type marked on the type plate.

final.answer: The item directly upstream of BV-10-1 is TV-10-2, a globe valve whose datasheet is a Fisher ET. A Fisher ET is a complete control valve, not just the valve body — the datasheet describes it as a single-port, globe-style control valve with cage guiding, a balanced valve plug, and push-down-to-close action, consisting of the body plus trim, bonnet and other parts. It is a globe-style (globe-type) control valve, used for throttling or on-off control of a wide variety of liquids and gases. (Its related variants are the EAT angle-body version and the ETR push-down-to-open version.)

final.answer: FT-10-1 (a Rosemount 3051) does not have a fixed failure direction — the output on failure is user-selectable, either high or low. The factory default ships with alarm = High (≥ 21.75 mA for HART 4-20 mA output; ≥ 22.5 mA for some options), with Low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA. To change the direction: for the HART 4-20 mA output (code A), select high or low failure mode with a jumper/switch on the transmitter; for the 1-5 Vdc low-power output (code M), select the alarm direction with an internal jumper (failure levels there are below 0.94 V for low or above 5.4 V for high). The direction can also be set at ordering via option codes C4/CN (NAMUR-compliant: high ≥ 22.5 mA, low ≤ 3.6 mA), CR/CS (custom levels: high 20.2–23.0 mA, low 3.6–3.8 mA, with the low alarm 0.1 mA below low saturation and the high alarm 0.1 mA above high saturation), or CT (Rosemount standard low). Note: for digital outputs (Fieldbus/PROFIBUS/wireless), no high/low analog drive applies — a failure is passed as an alert and status with the process variable.

final.answer: The valve operated by FIC-11-1 is FV-11-1 (a Fisher ET valve). Its datasheet lists the following plug seal ring materials and temperature limits (Table 14, p. 20). For the 2-piece valve plug seal (standard for NPS 1–6 except Cavitrol III cages): carbon-filled PTFE, −73 to 232 °C (−100 to 450 °F); ethylene-propylene, −40 to 232 °C (−40 to 450 °F), resists hot water/steam but not petroleum-based fluids/hydrocarbons; fluorocarbon, −18 to 204 °C (0 to 400 °F), for high-temperature air, hydrocarbons and some chemicals/solvents, not for steam, ammonia, or water above 82 °C; nitrile (air and hydrocarbons), −40 to 71 °C (−40 to 160 °F); nitrile (other compatible fluids), −40 to 82 °C (−40 to 180 °F). For the spring-loaded valve plug seal (standard for NPS 8 and Cavitrol III cages, optional otherwise): PTFE with N10276 spring, −73 to 232 °C (−100 to 450 °F); PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring (with PEEK anti-extrusion rings), −73 °C up to 316 °C (600 °F) in non-oxidizing service or 260 °C (500 °F) in oxidizing service. Above 232 °C, PEEK anti-extrusion rings plus a spring-loaded seal ring are required. The datasheet does not use the term 'piston rings'; it covers plug seal rings, anti-extrusion rings and backup/retaining rings. For Class VI shutoff trims the seal ring is UHMWPE, limited to −29 to 66 °C (17-4 SST cage) or −198 to 66 °C (316 SST/ENC cage).

Based on the facts found, here is what the datasheet says.

**Noise and cavitation purpose:** The easy-e family description states that the Whisper Trim and WhisperFlo cages provide aerodynamic noise attenuation, while the Cavitrol III cages provide cavitation protection (cavitation = the damaging bubble formation that occurs at high pressure drop) [p. 2]. So for noise, the Whisper trims (Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim, WhisperFlo) are the noise-reducing options, and for cavitation it is the Cavitrol III cage.

Tool result:
Datasheet rosemount-3051-00813-0100-4001, pages [80, 33, 28, 22, 32, 62, 39, 94]:
No — the facts found in this datasheet do not cover transmitter placement relative to pressure taps/orifice taps, and there is no installation guidance for gas service (e.g. mounting above the line so liquid does not collect). I could not find in these facts anything about where to mount the transmitter relative to the taps or about gas-versus-liquid impulse-line arrangement.

What the datasheet does contain, in case it is close to what you need:

- **Mounting position effects (Table 1, p. 80):** changing the mounting orientation only causes a "zero shift" (a small offset in the reading), not a span effect. Zero shifts are: Rosemount 3051C up to ±1.25 in H2O (3.11 mbar); 3051CA and 3051T ±2.5 in H2O (6.22 mbar); 3051L ±1 in H2O (2.49 mbar) with the liquid-level diaphragm in a vertical plane, ±5 in H2O (12.43 mbar) with the diaphragm in a horizontal plane, plus the extension length on extended units. All of these zero shifts can be calibrated out. This tells you how mounting orientation affects the reading — not where to mount relative to the taps.
- **Mounting brackets and dimensions:** bracket option codes (B1/B2/B3, B4/BE, B7/B8/B9 for flange mounting, p. 94) and mounting-configuration figures — Figure 11 on p. 99 (coplanar flange on a panel or 2-in. pipe with the optional B4 bracket, with dimensions and bolt sizes), Figure 14 on p. 101 (traditional flange with brackets B1/B7/BA, B2/B8 or B3/B9/BC), and Figure 19 on p. 104 (3051T bracket mounting on pipe or panel).
